summary.text: A 55-year-old Asian male patient with normal tension glaucoma had been using a tafluprost and timolol fixed combination; IOP was 14 mmHg in the right eye and 16 mmHg in the left eye by Goldmann applanation tonometry. Because of insufficient IOP control, the medication was switched to a brimonidine and timolol fixed combination.

Three months later IOP was 11 mmHg in the right eye and 10 mmHg in the left eye. Mild bilateral conjunctival injection and follicular conjunctivitis were noted, without discharge or membranous formation. Olopatadine was prescribed for a clinical impression of ocular allergic reaction without improvement after 2 weeks. Multiple bilateral corneal subepithelial infiltrates were seen, without epithelial defect or neovascularization.

Brimonidine was discontinued and topical fluorometholone and cyclosporine were prescribed. Four days after discontinuation the infiltrates improved markedly in both eyes, and one week after discontinuation they had completely resolved. Fluorometholone and cyclosporine were then tapered.
